title: n
The title of a book, movie, song, etc. is its name.
I just finished the best book." "Really, what's the title?
n
A title is a word or name that describes a person's job or status.
His title was Director of Science Education.
n
A title is a legal document that proves you own something.
He put the title to his house in a bank for safe keeping.
v
To give a title to someone or something.
I titled my essay "The History of Japan".
tired: If you feel tired, you have no energy and you need a rest.
After walking for 15 km, I was so tired, that I couldn't take another step.
ticket: A ticket is a piece of paper that allows you to enter a train, airplane, show, etc.
I bought my ticket to Mexico last week, but now I can't find it.
A ticket is a piece of paper that shows that you have parked your car in the wrong place or committed some other driving offence.
The policeman gave me a ticket for going 125 km/h.
If you ticket someone, then you give someone a ticket for breaking a law.
The officer ticketed the driver after he drove through a red light.
time: Time is what we measure with a clock.
What time do you finish work?" "At four o'clock (4:00).
If you do something one time, you do it once.
If you time something, you measure how long it takes in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Take out your watch and time yourself during the test.
tin: The kind of metal that cans are frequently made with. It is the chemical element Sn.
A can; a metal thing with food in it.
tie: If you tie something, you attach it using string or rope.
I was six when I learned to tie up my shoes.
If two teams or players tie, they have the same score in a game.
Naples and Rome tied the game two all.
A tie is a piece of cloth that you wear around your neck as a decoration.
At work, you need to wear a suit and tie.
tight: If x is tight, it fits closely and strongly to y.
The bandage on your finger should not be too tight or your finger may turn blue.
If a string is tight its ends are as far apart as possible.
A tight rope is in a straight line.
If you close or tie something tight, you do it strongly or closely so that it won't change easily.
He closed the door tight behind them.
till: In a period of time ending at a time someone says.
We will tell stories till it is time to sleep.
To make the earth ready for seeds.
A till is cash register; a machine which counts sales in shops and stores the money.
The till contained one hundred dollars at the end of the day
times: Three times three is nine" is written: 3 × 3 = 9.
tickle: When you tickle someone, you touch them in a way that makes them laugh.
He tickled Nancy's tummy, and she started to giggle.
tiger: A tiger is a mammal. It comes from Asia.
I'm going to take the kids to the zoo to see a tiger.
tit: A small bird of the genus ' or the family that is common in the northern hemisphere.
She's got an amazing pair of tits.
Look at that tit driving on the wrong side of the road!
* 1759, he was resolved, for the time to come, to ride his tit with more sobriety. — Laurence Sterne, The Life & Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman (Penguin 2003, p. 28)
A young girl, especially a hussy.
timer: A timer is a device that times something.
tibet: Tibet is a province of China. The capital is Lhasa.
tiresome: If someone or something is tiresome, it makes you bored or annoyed, usually because it is too long.
All of this talking can get a little tiresome.
tire: A tire is the outer part of a car wheel. It is usually made of rubber
The front tire on my bike needs changing.
tiny: Something that is tiny is very small.
A single grain of sand is tiny.
tick: A tick is a mark, used to show that something is right.
The teacher put a tick on the correct answer.
A tick is a small bug.
The dog was scratching because it had a tick in its ear.
A tick is a clicking noise that keeps going.
It was very quiet, and the only sound she could hear was the tick of the old clock.
A tick is small line used to show a measure or a count.
If something ticks, it is making clicking noises.
The clocked ticked on as I waited.
tidy: If something is tidy, it is clean and everything is in its place.
Her small, tidy, little house seemed very nice.
A tidy person is somebody who keeps thing clean and organized.
A tidy amount is not small.
They're planning to sell them for a tidy profit.
If you tidy something up, you pick up things and put everything back where it belongs.
Give me a minute to go tidy up the room.
tile: A tile is a hard flat building material, usually made of clay or glass.
The new floor would be ceramic tile, and the tiles on the walls were being replaced.
If you tile a surface, you cover it with tiles.
tip: n
The tip of something is the farthest point of it.
She runs her finger down the bird's back and to the tip of its tail.
n
A tip is words or ideas that help you solve a problem.
Police say anonymous tips have led them to more than 20 of the stolen items.
n
A tip is a small amount of money that you give to somebody to thank them for good service.
n
If something is the tip of the iceberg, it is just a small part of something much bigger.
The problems we've seen today are just the tip of the iceberg.
n
If something is on the tip of your tongue, you feel that you know it, but you can't say it.
I wanted the words to come out; They were on the tip of my tongue, but my mind still wasn't clear.
v
If something tips, the top of it moves to one side more than the bottom.
The piano tipped over as we were putting it on the truck.
v
If you tip something into something else, you pour it.
He tipped the water out of the glass by accident.
v
If you tip somebody, you give them money to thank them for good service.
v
If you tip somebody off, you tell them about something that's going to happen.
The police were tipped off by a phone call.
v
If you tip your hat, you touch it or pick it up when you meet or leave somebody.
v
If you tip your hat to somebody, you thank or congratulate them.
tinfoil: Tinfoil is a piece of tin which is flat and thin like paper. Sometimes people say "tinfoil" when they really mean "aluminium foil", which is made of a different metal, aluminium, instead of tin.
tilde: A punctuation character used in some different languages.
Tilde is used in the Spanish word piñata.
Wikimedia's projects use tildes to sign comments on talk pages.
tissue: A piece of tissue is a sheet of paper that can absorb very well.
He used the tissue I gave him to blow his nose.
Tissue is a group of cells that work together to do a job.
The human body is made up of many tissues, one example being muscle tissue.
tint: In color theory, a tint is the mixture of a color with white, which increases lightness.
If you tint something, you color or shade it.
The windows of the car are tinted.
timetable: A timetable is a kind of schedule with times of when the events are going to happen, usually used by schools to schedule lesson times.
Check the timetable to know what the next lesson is.
titanium: Titanium is a metallic (meaning made of metal) element with an atomic number of 22 and the symbol Ti.
Titanium is a strong and light metal which is used to build airplanes.
timber: Timber is trees and forests used as a source of wood.
They walked into the tall timber to find a place to camp.
Timber is wood used for building.
He went to the timber yard to buy the wood for his house.
Timber is a piece of wood used in building.
She carefully chose a timber that had an interesting pattern.
Timber is wood used as a frame in building ships.
During the battle he could feel the ship's timbers shiver.
To timber is to use wood as a support or frame.
The miners had to timber the shaft in the gold mine to make it safe.
timbre: Timbre is the qualities of a sound that make sounds different.
Even if a flute and saxophone play the same note, they sound different because of the timbre.
tide: The tide is the regular rising and falling of sea levels caused by the moon.
After getting the ship stuck on sand, the crew had to wait until high tide so it would refloat.
A tide may be something that rises and falls as if it were the sea.
The politicians knew that one day the tide of public opinion would agree with them.
Tide is a period of time or a season; usually used with another word.
She always looked forward to Whitsun tide.
tittle: A tittle is a small mark, like the little dot over i or j.
Don't forget to dot your is by adding tittles!
A tittle is a small amount of something, like a crumb or a speck.
tirumala: Tirumala is a city in the southern part of India
tights: Tights are pants worn by females that cover from the waist down to the feet.
tibetan: A Tibetan is a native or inhabitant of Tibet.
A Tibetan is a person of Tibetan ancestry.
tilt: If something tilts, it moves to one side.
The aeroplane was tilting to the left.
The tilt of an object is the position or movement of that object.
The aeroplane's tilt was to the left.
tighten: If you tighten something, you make it tighter.
Can you tighten the lid on the jar so it doesn't leak?
timeout: In sports a timeout is when the coach asks for a short stop in the game to talk with the team.
The coach of the home team is asking for a timeout.
A timeout is a short period to relax from a situation that causes stress.
I need a timeout from this meeting.
time-out: In sports a time-out is when the coach asks for a short stop in the game to talk with the team.
The coach of the home team is asking for a time-out.
A time-out is a short period to relax from a situation that causes stress.
I need a time-out from this meeting.
timid: If a person is timid, he or she does not have the courage or confidence to complete something.
tirade: A tirade is a long and angry criticism against a person.
tightly: If something is wrapped tightly, it is wrapped in a tight manner.
tier: A tier is one of a number of levels or layers.
She's from a top tier school.
A tier is somebody whose job is to tie something.
titular: Something in a work that is titular shares a name with the work's title.
is the titular character of the television show .
tipsy: If a person is tipsy, they are slightly drunk from drinking alcoholic beverages.
tiptoe: If a person tiptoes, they walk quietly with only the tips of the toes touching the ground.
tidiness: Tidiness is the quality of being tidy.
tingle: If a person tingles, they feel a slight sensation.
A tingle is a prickling or mildly stinging sensation.
timely: If something is done timely, it is done within the proper time limits.
tinhorn: A tinhorn is a person who pretends to have money, influence, or ability to do something.
tinkle: If something tinkles, it makes a light metallic sounds like a small bell.
A tinkle is a light metallic sound that resembles the tinkling of bells.
tightness: The tightness of something is how tight it is.
tiredness: Someone's tiredness is how tired they are.
timeless: If something is timeless, it never goes out of style or loses its importance.
The story's message is timeless and still relevant today.
If something is timeless, it exists outside of time or is not affected by time.
The beauty of the mountains seemed timeless.
titrate: If you titrate a solution, you determine the amount of a substance in it by measuring the volume of a known concentration of reagent that is needed to complete a reaction with it.
A titrate is solution containing an unknown concentration of substance which is to be tested by titration.
tianjin: Tianjin is a city in northern China.
tilak: A tilak is a mark worn on the forehead, traditionally in Hindu cultures, often made with substances such as sandalwood paste, ash, or colored powder.
titration: Titration is a laboratory method used to determine the concentration of a substance in a solution by adding a solution of known concentration until a reaction reaches its endpoint.
